transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, my supervisor suggested I come in. It’s mostly because... ever since I got this county safety award a little while back, things have just been really off. They actually did this whole dinner for the award, which was nice, I guess, except the chicken they served was incredibly dry. Like, you needed a whole glass of water just to get one bite down. And the venue they picked was right next to the old rail yard, which is funny because I inspect the new transit buses and light rail cars. The suspension on those new models is a total nightmare to check, you have to get right under the chassis and the clearance is terrible. 

But anyway, since I got that award, certain people at work have been taking my inspection reports and twisting them around. They keep asking me all these really pointed budget questions, basically trying to make it look like I’m crooked or doing something shady with the maintenance logs. My supervisor keeps telling me it’s just a normal review process and I shouldn't worry about it. Normal review, right. I mean, I had to replace my water heater at my house last week because the pilot light kept going out, and the plumber tried to overcharge me for a basic pressure valve, so I know when someone's trying to pull a fast one on me. I can just tell there’s a coordinated effort to discredit me at the depot, no matter what my boss says.
Since when exactly have you noticed these thoughts that coworkers are coordinating against you—how many weeks or months has this been going on?

Well, let's see... it’s been about a year now. Yeah, right around twelve months, ever since I got recognized for that county safety initiative I was talking about. They actually gave me this really heavy glass plaque for it. I tried putting it on my desk at home, but the way my window faces, the sun hits it right around 3 PM and creates this blinding glare right in my eyes. 

I ended up having to move it to this little bookshelf in the hallway. I bought that shelf at Ikea, actually, and man, it took me like three hours to put together because they forgot to put those little wooden dowels in the box. I had to drive all the way back out to the store just to get them, and the traffic on the interstate was backed up for miles because of a fender bender near the exit. People just do not know how to zipper merge anymore, I swear. It's like they see a "lane closed ahead" sign and just panic and slam on the brakes, you know? It really messes up the flow of everything.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to notice or hear?

No, I don't hear voices or anything like that. My hearing is completely normal. Actually, it's probably better than normal, which is exactly why I picked up on this weird rattling noise in my truck last Tuesday. It sounded like it was coming from right behind the steering column, you know? But when I took it into the shop, the guy tried to tell me it was the serpentine belt. 

I mean, come on. I inspect heavy transit vehicles for a living, I know exactly what a worn belt sounds like. It's a high-pitched squeal, not a metallic rattle. But he just wouldn't listen to me. It seems like mechanics nowadays just plug their little diagnostic tablet into the dashboard, and if the computer doesn't spell it out for them, they have absolutely no idea what to do. My uncle used to rebuild classic cars, mostly old Chevelles and Mustangs, and he could figure out an engine problem just by putting a long screwdriver against the block and listening to the vibrations through the handle. He had this gorgeous '68 Mustang, dark green, kind of like the one in that Steve McQueen movie. He spent three years restoring the interior alone because he insisted on finding the exact original leather for the seats.
Aside from these concerns about coworkers, has there been any change in how well you're able to do your job, take care of daily tasks, or interact with family and friends over this past year?

No, everything else is fine. I still get to work on time, I complete all my transit inspections, I keep up with church on Sundays, and I take care of myself. It's really just when people bring up those reports or start questioning my spending that the problems start. But speaking of church, the new pastor they brought in last month is really changing things up. He decided we needed to update the hymnals, which is fine, but the new ones they ordered have this really weird font that's almost impossible to read from a distance. 

My aunt Helen used to play the organ there, actually. She played for almost forty years before her arthritis got too bad. She had this beautiful old Hammond organ in her living room, too, with the full pedalboard and everything. I used to go over there on Sundays after service and she'd let me mess around with the drawbars. She always had these little hard strawberry candies in a crystal dish on top of it. You know the ones, with the wrappers that look like actual strawberries? I tried to find those at the grocery store the other day because I was feeling nostalgic, but all they had were those generic mints. The candy aisle at that store is a disaster anyway, half the shelves are always empty, and the prices are just ridiculous now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that coworkers are coordinating to discredit him via manipulated inspection reports and budget questions) that has persisted for approximately 12 months. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech pattern rising to formal thought disorder (though marked tangentiality/circumstantiality is present), and no negative symptoms. Critically, occupational and social functioning remain intact outside the delusional theme—he continues to work, attend church, and manage self-care. This pattern of an isolated, encapsulated delusion with preserved functioning outside the delusional system, in the absence of prominent hallucinations or disorganization, is most consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22), persecutory type, rather than Schizophrenia (which requires broader functional decline and/or additional first-rank psychotic symptoms) or Schizotypal disorder.
